_what: D187 Task 2: has anything on the LIVE PATH of `streamscout` or `lmcache` changed since their s4/s5 cells were produced? Asked because s6/s7 cells are wanted and would be compared against those s4/s5 cells.
_register: Two registers, kept apart. (1) A STATIC CLOSURE DIFF over the module-level import closure, which is a CONSTRUCTED BOUND: it reports every file that changed, including files these arms never execute. (2) An EMPIRICAL DRY DIGEST, which is an OBSERVED comparison: the same arm, same workload, same seed, run on a clean checkout of the cell's own revision and of origin/main. The digest is the one that answers 'could a decision move'; the closure diff alone cannot, because arms_published.py imports every baseline adapter at module level, so an unrelated arm's change lands in the closure of both arms.
_tree: every cell ran on a CLEAN checkout containing ONLY committed code, built with `git archive`, NOT in the shared worktree, which carries other sessions' uncommitted edits.
_instrument_unchanged: hybrid/test_hybrid.py (the dry harness) and fleet/trace.py (the workload generator) are BYTE-IDENTICAL between both compared revisions and origin/main, so a digest difference would be the live path and not the instrument.

step1_revision_of_each_cell._how: read from each cell's OWN run_meta.json and header.json (they agree)
step1_revision_of_each_cell.FINDING_TWO_REVISIONS_ARE_UNREACHABLE: `50777f0d` (streamscout s5) and `4af40941` (lmcache s4) exist NEITHER locally NOR on origin: `git fetch origin <sha>` returns `upload-pack: not our ref` for both. They were never pushed, or were pushed on a history since rewritten. Each cell's header records a CLEAN tree at that sha, so the code state was a real committed state -- it is simply not recoverable. THEREFORE those two cells' own revisions CANNOT be diffed, and what is reported for them is a BOUND from the commit that ADDED the cell to git, not the cell's revision. This is a register distinction, not a technicality: the s4/s5 pair is half unverifiable.

step2_static_closure_diff.note: the two arms' closures are IDENTICAL (85 files), because arms_published.py imports every baseline adapter at module level.

step2_static_closure_diff.why_the_changed_files_are_gated: the coordinator additions (+532/-7 since ef4a963a) are the D178/D179 share-admission and release-recheck work. Both are gated on INSTANCE attributes that default False (`share_admission.arm_enables` / `release_recheck.arm_enables`, which RAISE on a truthy class attribute), and `coordinator._share_ok` returns True unchanged when the switch is off. A repo-wide grep shows `live2_share_admission` and `live2_release_recheck` are set ONLY in d179_release_recheck_proofs.py and d179_share_tests.py -- never in arms_published.py, never for these two arms. The one ungated addition in `_expire` is a MEASUREMENT MIRROR whose decision-bearing half sits under `if self._share_admission`. streamscout_adapted.py does not import cascade_adapted, so that change cannot reach it. hybrid/hybrid_arm.py is executed only by hybrid-* arms. THIS IS A READING OF THE CODE AND IS WEAKER THAN A MEASUREMENT, which is why step 3 exists.
